html:
Wife of the emperor Justinian I and empress from 527 to her death in 548, one of the most powerful women in Roman history. She was born in Constantinople to a bear keeper of the racing factions at the Hippodrome and worked as an actress, a job with a low reputation.

Justinian fell for her, and a law was changed so that a man of his rank could marry a former actress. As empress she took a real part in government:

  • During the Nika riots of 532, by Procopius's account, she persuaded Justinian not to flee, saying that royalty makes a fine burial shroud.
  • She protected Christians who rejected Chalcedon, the Miaphysites, even sheltering some in the palace.
  • She backed laws against forced prostitution and for women's rights in marriage and property.

She died in 548, probably of cancer. Her portrait with her court survives in the mosaics of San Vitale in Ravenna. Procopius's Secret History paints her as wicked, and that hostile picture shaped her image for centuries.
